preparation_rules: Never apply heat: Cooking or boiling causes vesicles to burst and collapse instantly.
Wash immediately before serving: Rinse in cool, clean water right before assembling.
Dress immediately prior to eating: Acid and salt extract water from the beads through osmosis within 5-10 minutes.

recipes.title: Classic Filipino Ensaladang Lato (Seaweed Salad)
recipes.description: A classic side dish pairing crisp sea grapes with diced tomatoes, onions, and optional salted duck egg.
ingredients: 2 large ripe plum tomatoes (cored and finely diced)
1 piece salted duck egg (itlog na maalat, peeled and diced, optional)
1 thumb-sized piece fresh ginger (peeled and minced, optional)
3 tbsp cane vinegar or coconut vinegar
1 tbsp fresh calamansi juice or lime juice
instructions: Place fresh lato in a bowl of cold water. Gently pick out debris, sea stones, or damaged stems. Drain thoroughly.
Submerge the cleaned lato in a bowl of ice water for 2 to 3 minutes to maximize crispness. Drain well.
In a separate bowl, whisk together the vinegar, calamansi juice, sugar, and cracked black pepper until the sugar dissolves. Stir in the diced tomatoes, red onions, and ginger.
Place the drained lato on a serving platter and top with the salted egg. Either pour the dressing over the top immediately before serving or serve the dressing on the side as a dip.

recipes.title: Okinawan Umi-Budo with Citrus Ponzu Dip
recipes.description: Fresh sea grapes served unadorned over crushed ice with a citrusy, savory ponzu dipping sauce.
ingredients: 1.5 tbsp yuzu juice, sudachi juice, or fresh lemon juice
instructions: Submerge umi-budo in clean, room-temperature or cool water for 1 to 2 minutes to reduce residual salinity. Drain completely.
Whisk together soy sauce, yuzu juice, dashi, mirin, and rice vinegar in a small dip ramekin.
Bed a plate with crushed ice, lay the fresh umi-budo clusters on top, and place the ponzu bowl alongside.
Dip individual fronds into the sauce right before biting. Avoid pouring the dip over the seaweed to keep the pearls firm.

recipes.title: Okinawan Umi-Budo Donburi (Sea Grape & Sashimi Rice Bowl)
recipes.description: A popular Izakaya rice bowl where sea grapes act as a popping textural contrast to fresh raw sashimi.
ingredients: 150 g sushi-grade yellowfin tuna or salmon (sliced for sashimi)
2 cups cooked Japanese short-grain rice (cooled to room temp)
1 piece egg yolk or poached/onsen egg (optional)
instructions: Gently fold seasoned rice vinegar into the cooked rice. Allow it to cool slightly so heat does not collapse the sea grapes.
Quick-rinse umi-budo in cool water and pat dry with paper towels.
Divide rice into two serving bowls. Lay shiso leaves on top, arrange sashimi slices along one side, and pile fresh umi-budo on the other side. Nest-egg the yolk in the center if desired.
Serve with wasabi and soy sauce on the side.

recipes.title: Malaysian Latok with Sambal Belacan & Calamansi
recipes.description: Fresh sea grapes paired with a spicy, citrusy, and savory pounded shrimp paste dip.
ingredients: 2 pieces fresh red bird's eye chilies (cili padi)
instructions: Wash latok thoroughly in clean water 2 to 3 times to remove any remaining sand or grit. Drain in a colander.
In a mortar and pestle, pound the chilies, toasted belacan, shallot, sugar, and salt into a textured paste. Squeeze the juice of two calamansi limes into the paste and stir.
Place the latok on a plate alongside extra calamansi halves and the sambal belacan dip. Dip the sea grapes into the sambal before eating.

recipes.title: Sesame-Soy & Cucumber Sea Grape Salad
recipes.description: A crisp, modern cold salad featuring julienned cucumber, cherry tomatoes, and toasted sesame dressing.
ingredients: 1 piece Japanese or Persian cucumber (thinly julienned)
instructions: Whisk sesame oil, soy sauce, lemon juice, and honey in a bowl. Toss julienned cucumber and cherry tomatoes with half of the dressing.
Rinse sea grapes in cold water, dunk in an ice bath for 2 minutes, then drain thoroughly.
Arrange the dressed vegetables on a plate, lay the sea grapes across the top, drizzle with the remaining dressing right before serving, and sprinkle with toasted sesame seeds.
